title: Global-profile version OCC (in-project coarse reference arm)
algorithm_class: coarse-grained optimistic concurrency control (single global version profile per entity class)
supported_guarantee: Commits are admitted only if one global profile epoch is unchanged at validation time; any concurrent write anywhere in the profile invalidates every in-flight transaction
limitations_vs_candidate: Validates a single global epoch so it cannot distinguish semantically required cross-resource reads from incidental profile activity; this over-aborts (false-stale rejections) and it models no consent/policy epochs as part of the validated dependency set so it cannot answer RQ1 or RQ2
mechanism_analysis: Strong comparator because it is the coarsest scope-local OCC an industrial deployment would actually ship: it shares the candidate's commit-time-validation skeleton but has the widest possible validation scope, so it upper-bounds the false-stale rate that dependency scoping is claimed to reduce and is the directly named counterfactual in RQ1.

title: Speedy Transactions in Multicore In-Memory Databases (Silo)
algorithm_class: Silo-style optimistic concurrency control with per-entity readset validation and commit-time epoch batching (faithful port of published algorithm; not Silo source code)
supported_guarantee: Serializable optimistic concurrency: per-entity versioned reads with local buffers and commit-time validation against epoch/version fences (Tu et al. 2013 Sec. 3-4)
limitations_vs_candidate: Validates exactly the read sets the workload declares; it does not derive the semantically required cross-resource dependency closure per clinical write operation and it binds no consent/policy epochs into the validated set so omitted-dependency flaws (write skew and policy-epoch races) remain outside its validation contract
mechanism_analysis: Strong algorithmic comparator because per-entity readset OCC is the strongest published OCC shape that could plausibly deliver the same abort reduction without semantic dependency derivation: it shares commit-time validation and version fences with the candidate while differing precisely in the derived-versus-declared read-set axis that RQ1 isolates.

title: Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL
algorithm_class: serializable snapshot isolation (SSI) database-native concurrency control with predicate locking (SIReadLock SIREAD conflict tracking)
supported_guarantee: True serializability: concurrent Serializable transactions commit only if some serial order produces the same effect; anomaly monitoring adds no blocking beyond repeatable read (verified in PostgreSQL 16 docs Sec. 13.2.3 citing ports12)
limitations_vs_candidate: Provides general serializability without deriving semantic dependency closures and its anomaly monitoring is opaque to clinical semantics (consent/policy epochs are enforced only as ordinary predicates inside transactions); the candidate claims no new isolation level only a measured safety/throughput frontier against this sound DB-native reference
mechanism_analysis: Strong DB-native comparator because it is the soundness reference the whole frontier is measured against: any forbidden-commit safety the candidate achieves must be achievable by SSI plus schema-check predicates, and RQ3's crossover point is defined relative to its throughput, so a weak version of this arm would invalidate the paper's central trade-off.

title: Entity-OCC without semantic dependency closure (ablation of the candidate)
algorithm_class: ablation: entity-level OCC without semantic dependency closure (write-skew exposing control)
supported_guarantee: Same commit-time per-entity validation as B1 but with the dependency-closure derivation disabled; expected to admit write-skew and policy-epoch-race histories
limitations_vs_candidate: It is a controlled degradation of the candidate not an external system: it exists to expose the anomaly families (write skew; policy-epoch races) whose oracle detection rates define RQ2 endpoints, so it must never be presented as a full external comparator
mechanism_analysis: Strong comparator by ablation design: it isolates the single mechanism axis (semantic dependency closure) between itself and the candidate, which is exactly the falsification instrument RQ2 needs to attribute detected write-skew propagation to the omitted dependency rather than to any other feature difference.

title: Dependency-complete optimistic admission for concurrent clinical AI writes (candidate)
algorithm_class: dependency-complete scope-local optimistic concurrency control with per-operation derived dependency closure and consent/policy epoch validation
supported_guarantee: Commits are admitted only when every derived semantically required cross-resource edge (medication/allergy/history/purpose grants plus consent and policy epochs) validates in one DB transaction under canonical lock ordering; forbidden commits under complete independently labeled schedules must remain zero and false-stale rejections must drop versus B0/B1
limitations_vs_candidate: Is the object under study so it has no limitations-vs-candidate by definition; its claims are falsifiable per blueprint (any forbidden commit under a complete independently labeled schedule falsifies the safety claim; if fully serializable PostgreSQL is as fast the null performance benefit is candidly reported)
mechanism_analysis: The candidate anchors the matrix: every other row states its limitation relative to this arm's derived dependency closure and two-sided frontier, and its own guarantee is stated falsifiably so the study can fail honestly.

title: Elle: Inferring Isolation Anomalies from Experimental Observations
algorithm_class: independent black-box transaction-history checker (anomaly inference from exported histories)
supported_guarantee: Infers isolation anomalies from experimentally observed histories without candidate introspection; black-box contract of histories-in anomalies-out
limitations_vs_candidate: Does not derive clinical dependency closures or admit writes; it adjudicates exported histories after the fact so it supplies the independent oracle contract (RQ2 adjudication) but no admission mechanism to compare throughput against
mechanism_analysis: Strong comparator for evidence independence because the entire adjudication story (truthful export judged by a checker that never imports candidate code) rests on its black-box contract; using it as-is forecloses the self-reported-success failure mode and supplies the history-checking half of the independent-oracle requirement.

title: Zanzibar: Google's Consistent, Global Authorization System
algorithm_class: consistency-aware distributed fine-grained authorization (ReBAC with revision staleness bounded by latency knobs)
supported_guarantee: Globally consistent permission evaluation with bounded staleness of the ACL view (external consistency of permission state)
limitations_vs_candidate: Governs permission consistency at read/evaluation time not transactional commit admission under concurrent resource mutation; a pure permission re-evaluation cannot reproduce the candidate's read-set closure so it tests novelty beyond permission re-checks (falsification row F5)
mechanism_analysis: Strong comparator because it is the industrial-grade answer to the question of why not just re-check permissions at commit time: its bounded-staleness consistency model is the closest non-transactional alternative to epoch validation and the candidate must show dependency validation does something permission re-evaluation cannot.

title: Macaroons: Cookies with Contextual Caveats for Decentralized Authorization in the Cloud
algorithm_class: caveat-bound HMAC bearer credentials with delegation attenuation and third-party caveats
supported_guarantee: Unforgeable contextual attenuation: caveats are cryptographically bound so they cannot be stripped and verification fails closed on unknown or false caveats
limitations_vs_candidate: Contextual caveats constrain capabilities at authorization time but do not version-check mutable resources at commit time so caveat re-derivation alone cannot prevent write skew between capability issuance and resource mutation (falsification row F5)
mechanism_analysis: Strong comparator because caveat-bound tokens are the strongest capability-based mechanism for carrying consent/policy context into a decision and the candidate must demonstrate that epochs inside a validated dependency set catch races that caveat re-derivation at commit time cannot.
